author: Michael Larabel
description: Wine 11.22 is out today as the latest bi-weekly development release and inching quite closely toward the Wine 12.0 stable release preparations...
title: Wine 11.22 Introduces x86 AVX Emulation On ARM64

author: Michael Larabel
description: Earlier this year Cloudflare announced Kitesurf as a stateless web browser for AI agents. After building out its features, they have now made good on their word to open-source it...
title: Cloudflare Open Sources Kitesurf: Their Web Browser For AI Agents

author: Michael Larabel
description: Since 2023 I and many open-source advocates have been very eager for AMD's openSIL project for delivering open-source CPU silicon initialization as a replacement to the traditional AGESA code. With Zen 5 there was proof-of-concept support that we have enjoyed with Coreboot on an MSI Ryzen motherboard and a Gigabyte EPYC server motherboard thanks to the Coreboot-based Dasharo ports by 3mdeb. The goal for production readiness was for Zen 6, but with this week's EPYC 9006 SP7 announcement the openSIL topic wasn't touched on. So I asked around...
title: AMD openSIL Achieves Its Production Goal With 6th Gen EPYC "Venice"

author: Michael Larabel
description: KDE Frameworks 6.32 shipped today as the newest monthly update to this set of KDE components. Notable this month is a fix for the previously-reported 15 year old bug around inaccurate notifications for USB file transfers...
title: KDE Frameworks 6.32 Released With That Fix For USB File Transfer Notifications

author: Michael Larabel
description: Following the recent release of HRX Loom v0.1 and leveraging an AI agent workflow, a team at AMD experimented with bringing 50 trending Hugging Face models over to AMD client GPUs. They accomplished this feat in just around three days, thanks to their HRX software work paired with the power of Ryzen AI Max "Strix Halo" hardware...
title: AMD Leverages AI + HRX Loom In Experiment For Quickly Porting 50 LLMs To Client GPUs

author: Michael Larabel
description: A new tool expected to be merged to the Linux 7.5 source tree provides a new exercise for the kernel and in the process bringing down the system...
title: Linux 7.5 To Include New hwpoison-panic Tool For Intentionally Crashing Your System

author: Michael Larabel
description: In addition to AOCC 6.0 releasing this week as their updated C/C++ compiler along with the new "AOF" Fortran compiler, AMD also released AOCL 6.0 as the AMD Optimizing CPU Libraries...
title: AMD AOCL 6.0 Introduces New RNG Library, Initial Zen 6 CPU Optimizations

author: Michael Larabel
description: Longtime Linux developer Christoph Hellwig today announced the initial public release of XRAID. XRAID is a declustered parity RAID implementation integrated into the XFS file-system. XRAID is focused on RAID for zoned XFS deployments...
title: XRAID Publicly Released As New RAID Implementation For XFS

author: Michael Larabel
description: Sent out today was the drm-misc-next pull request for the week of new material to queue in DRM-Next until the Linux 7.5 merge window gets underway in late December. Most notable this week is the introduction of the new GlandaGPU driver...
title: Linux 7.5 To Upstream Driver For New Glanda GPU

author: Michael Larabel
description: One of the consistent wonderful praise I have for Intel over the past 22+ years of covering the Linux hardware scene has been their upstreaming of new CPU targets into the open-source compilers like GCC well ahead of product launches. Particularly with GCC on an annual feature release cycle and not being quickly picked up by new Linux distribution releases, Intel upstreaming their new CPU targets and ISA features at times years in advance of product releases has helped ensure smooth compiler ecosystem support by the time their products ship. The latest example, today they posted their patches providing new ISA features and enabling for both Coral Rapids and Razor Lake processors...
title: Intel Posts Initial GCC Compiler Code For Razor Lake & Coral Rapids

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Rust-based NVIDIA Linux kernel driver "Nova" is set to take on an important role in the official NVIDIA Linux driver stack of the future. This mainline kernel driver continues seeing a flurry of activity to bring it into a usable state and eventually parity and beyond compared to the existing out-of-tree NVIDIA Linux driver code or the incomplete and largely reverse engineered Nouveau kernel driver. Presented at this week's KVM Forum was the current status of NVIDIA bringing vGPU support to the upstream kernel...
title: NVIDIA Highlights Their Open-Source vGPU Upstreaming Work Built Atop Nova
